correctness.rationale: For all integers n at least five, apex-edge detours force every shadow; the only pairs detecting a given shadow-to-original edge force the selected original vertices to be a vertex cover. Explicit unique-geodesic witnesses prove sufficiency for all three edge types, including cyclic boundary cases. Independent-set and cyclic 2/3-gap enumeration yield both polynomials with exact integer coefficients, and maximum-independent-set swaps prove the parity-sensitive relocation graph. An independent original-graph/deleted-edge distance checker tested 698368 complete subsets for orders 5 through 9, their minimal sets and jumps/slides, plus shadow-pair certificates for orders 10 through 15. No finite result is substituted for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The Mycielski operation is a natural chromatic graph construction. The nontrivial equivalence reduces exactly all edge-failure monitoring arrangements to cyclic vertex covers, giving a complete infinite-family set enumerator, exact inclusion-minimal spectra, reentrant purity at n=7, and optimal relocations with a parity-dependent connected-versus-frozen dichotomy. These are structurally motivated facts about sensing redundancy and feasible movements, not an arbitrary finite sample.
